answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted reputation that grows slowly, like a trellis guiding a vine. Each new agent must lock a small bond and earn trust through peer-verified work across many epochs. A sybil farmer spinning up a meadow of fake identities must split capital among them, so each stays weak and easy to slash when peers catch collusion. Honest agents accumulate history as solid as marble, which cannot be bought overnight. Cost scales with identities, while rewards scale with genuine, long-term contribution.
